<reason>B convincingly distinguished comparable integration from comparable public benefit. A established genuine interests in family unity, but did not justify extending those interests into general priority beyond serious dependency. A also repeatedly invoked superior rootedness despite the stipulated comparability. B answered the pressure questions directly and showed why merely listing alternative staffing tools did not eliminate the opportunity cost of foregoing economic admissions.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s strongest response reframed the choice as residents’ family reunion versus other residents’ healthcare, not family belonging versus an economic applicant’s destination preference. This directly undermined A’s claimed moral asymmetry while preserving substantial protection for serious family hardship.</best_rebuttal>
